target.title: fix(telegram): silently skip empty-text sends
target.body:
Supersedes #59725 (auto-closed by the 10-open-PR cap; not reopenable because the close `stateReason` is `COMPLETED` and the branch was force-pushed since). ## Scope note: re-derived on top of current main Most of the original branch scope has since landed on `main` through other work, so this PR was reset onto `main` and re-implemented to cover only the residual gaps: - #56620 added `filterEmptyTelegramTextChunks` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.replies.ts`), which already drops whitespace-only chunks before any send. - The `sendTelegramText` rewrite around `sendPlainFallback` / `buildTelegramPlainFallbackPlan` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.ts`) already recovers formatted-send failures when a non-empty plain fallback exists. - #93279 introduced the default-vs-rich delivery split, which this PR preserves: the rich lane stays opt-in behind `richMessages === true` and both lanes get the same skip semantics. Two gaps remain on current `main`, and they are exactly the reported user path: 1. `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` only matches Telegram's legacy `message text is empty` wording. The live Bot API now also returns `text must be non-empty` (raw round-trip below), so the empty-text 400 escapes the recovery branch. 2. When non-whitespace source renders to empty visible text and the plain fallback is also empty (for example `` with `plainText: ""`), `main` throws (`empty rich text and empty plain fallback` / `empty formatted text and empty plain fallback`) or rethrows the 400 from the catch block, surfacing a user-visible delivery failure for content the model never made visible. ## Behavior addressed Interrupted mid-reply turns can produce formatted Telegram HTML that has no visible text and no plain-text fallback, for example an empty supported tag such as ``. Telegram rejects that payload with HTTP 400 (`message text is empty` legacy wording, `text must be non-empty` newer wording). Previously this surfaced as a user-visible delivery failure; this PR silently treats that empty-text send as a no-op with correct accounting. Parse errors remain out of scope and still throw (bare `
` payloads fail as parse errors, per the live baseline below). ## Change - `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` now also matches `text must be non-empty` and the rich-lane `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED` rejection. - `sendTelegramText` returns `Promise`: when the rendered payload is empty and the plain fallback is also empty, it resolves `undefined` (silent no-op) instead of throwing, both pre-flight and when Telegram rejects the payload as empty. Sends with a usable plain fallback still recover exactly as on `main`; parse errors and unrelated failures still throw. - `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` treats an `undefined` chunk result as a no-op: no `markReplyApplied`, no `markDelivered`, so skipped chunks do not advance reply state, delivered count, transcript mirroring, `message_sent.success`, or pinning. - Review fix (clawsweeper finding on the previous revision): in the suppressed single-use multi-chunk lane (the Telegram Desktop workaround in `reply-threading.ts`), the reply target is now consumed on the first delivered chunk instead of being keyed to chunk index 0. Previously a silently-skipped chunk 0 left `progress.hasReplied` false forever, leaking unconsumed single-use reply state to later sends in the same batch that share the delivery progress (`deliverReplies` creates one shared progress per batch). `markReplyApplied` is idempotent, so delivered chunks after the first are no-ops. - Voice fallback text paths mirror only text that actually reached Telegram: an all-skipped caption fallback no longer registers `reply.text` as delivered transcript content. ## Verification Run after this patch on the rebased head (current `main` d3ff48c51f + this commit): ``` node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/reply-threading.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts -> 4 files, 83 tests passed node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram -> 134 files, 2464 tests passed (the pre-rebase bot.test.ts failure noted in the previous revision no longer reproduces on current main) node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json -> clean node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json -> clean oxlint -> clean oxfmt --check -> clean ``` The new regression test (`reply-threading.test.ts`, skipped chunk 0 followed by two delivered chunks) fails on the previous revision with `expected [ false, false, false ] to deeply equal [ false, false, true ]` and passes with the fix; a second case pins that across separate single-chunk sends sharing progress, the reply target attaches to the first delivered send exactly once and skipped sends neither consume nor break the chain. ## Live Telegram round-trip Raw Telegram Bot API baseline (no OpenClaw code), re-run 2026-07-08 against the live Bot API: ``` payload="
" -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unsupported start tag \"br\" at byte offset 0" payload="" -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: text must be non-empty" payload="OpenClaw PR 88810 raw Bot API baseline: delivered reply" -> ok=true message_id=11323 ``` `tsx` driver importing the source-tree `sendTelegramText`, run on the exact rebased head `f5807ad1b2ca2b68c792151f7094b6ad70ddb8cd` against the live Bot API (token and chat id redacted): ``` [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage skipped chat=: Telegram rejected text as empty (Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: text must be non-empty)) (a) empty html + empty plain fallback -> resolved: undefined [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11324 (b) normal payload -> resolved message_id: 11324 ``` Second `tsx` driver on the same exact head exercising the fixed `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` single-use consumption lane live (chunk 0 renders empty and is skipped by Telegram, chunk 1 delivers, then a follow-up send shares the same delivery progress): ``` [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11325 anchor message_id: 11325 [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage skipped chat=: Telegram rejected text as empty (Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: text must be non-empty)) [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11326 multi-chunk batch: sendChunk replyToMessageId per chunk: [ undefined, undefined ] progress.hasReplied after skipped chunk 0 + delivered chunk 1: true [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11327 follow-up sendChunk replyToMessageId: [ undefined ] ``` The suppressed multi-chunk lane attaches the native reply param to no chunk by design (Telegram Desktop workaround); the state proof is `progress.hasReplied: true` after the first delivered chunk and the follow-up send not resurrecting the anchor reply target. ## Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: Empty visible-text Telegram HTML sends with an empty plain fallback no longer surface as delivery failures; they are treated as no-op sends with no phantom delivery accounting and no leaked single-use reply state, while parse errors and fallback-capable sends behave as on main. Real environment tested: Live Telegram Bot API on the exact rebased head f5807ad1b2ca2b68c792151f7094b6ad70ddb8cd (raw `sendMessage` curl baseline plus a `tsx` driver importing the source-tree `sendTelegramText` via grammY), and local Vitest runs of the rebased code. Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/reply-threading.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram`, and the live driver above on the exact head. Evidence after fix: 83/83 tests pass across the four delivery/reply test files, including the new consumption regression (skipped chunk 0 no longer strands `progress.hasReplied`); live Bot API on the exact head resolves `undefined` for `` with `plainText: ""` (logged as a skip, no throw) and returns a real `message_id` (11324) for a normal payload. Observed result after fix: Empty-text sends skip silently without advancing reply delivery state; the single-use reply target is consumed by the first delivered chunk even when earlier chunks skip; payloads with real content or a usable plain fallback deliver unchanged; bare `
` HTML still throws the Telegram parse error and remains out of scope. What was not tested: No full live interrupted-agent session was exercised; the live driver exercises `sendTelegramText` directly rather than the whole `deliverReplies` pipeline over a running gateway. Focused regression tests cover send skipping, reply accounting, single-use reply consumption, transcript mirroring, hooks, pin behavior, and voice fallback paths.
